title: RFI and negotiation toolkit for dedicated inference
content:
Purpose: This is a lightweight RFI / negotiation toolkit for commercial conversations where customers evaluate dedicated inference capacity (reserved GPU pools) and want procurement-ready answers covering SLAs, isolation, predictable throughput, and contract language. Use this doc to: 1) speed up replies to common RFP/RFI questions, 2) align Sales + Solutions on acceptable redlines/BATNA, and 3) provide engineers with exact items procurement will check.

Audience: Sales reps, solutions engineers (SEs), commercial legal reviewers, and product marketing owners supporting Dedicated capacity deals.

TL;DR messaging (one-liners for pitch and RFP answers):
- Predictable throughput: "Dedicated GPU pools with configurable autoscaling and burst to N additional nodes give you predictable sustained TPS and reserved capacity for peak windows."
- Isolation & data controls: "Logical and optional physical isolation (VPC peering + isolated clusters) so customer workloads and data remain separate; no co-tenancy on dedicated pools unless expressly negotiated."
- SLA & remedies: "Committed availability and latency SLOs backed by service credits and operational runbooks — can be tailored to committed throughput tiers."
- Procurement-ready: "We provide RFI answers, sample SOWs, and standard contract language for uptime, scaling, audit logs, and termination assistance to make procurement cycles fast and low friction."

Core offer elements to surface in RFIs (short bullets to paste into responses):
- Reserved capacity footprint: GPUs, RAM, NVMe sizing, expected token throughput per GPU for common models (we include calibrated numbers for popular open models).
- Autoscale policy and burst: baseline reserved nodes + configurable burst nodes (billing and lead times documented).
- Network & tenancy isolation: VPC/private endpoint, dedicated clusters, region pinning, E2E encryption, customer KMS integration.
- Observability & reporting: per-route latency percentiles, token-level billing, error rates, per-token cost breakdown.
- Incident response & escalation: 24/7 support for paid tiers, SRE contact, runbooks, and RCA cadence.
- Migration & onboarding: 30–90 day onboarding depending on scope, optional migration engineering hours.

Sample RFI answers (copy/paste friendly):
Q: What uptime and latency SLAs do you offer for dedicated capacity?
A: We offer a baseline SLA of 99.9% monthly uptime for the inference control plane and 99.5% for customer-dedicated GPU clusters. We publish p95 latency targets per model-family for a reference sequence length (e.g., p95 <= 120ms for 2k tokens on model X on rgpu-8). Remedies include service credits calculated as a percent of monthly committed fee for sustained violations; specific caps and thresholds are contract-dependent for enterprise deals.

Q: How do you provide isolation between tenants?
A: Dedicated offering includes per-customer GPU clusters with network isolation (VPC peering or PrivateLink), namespace-level RBAC, and optional physical isolation (single-tenant hosts) for regulated workloads. No data, KV cache, or runtime memory is shared across tenant clusters. We support KMS/HSM key management and thorough audit logs for all administrative and API-level operations.

Q: How do you guarantee predictable throughput during high load?
A: Predictability is achieved through reserved capacity sizing, autoscale windows, and request routing policies. For committed tiers we guarantee a minimum sustained tokens-per-second per cluster; we also provide burst capacity that can be configured (e.g., up to 2x baseline for 15-minute windows). We recommend customers pin critical routes to dedicated clusters and use our intelligent batching settings to maximize throughput and token-efficiency.

Technical appendix (engineer-friendly snippets to include in responses):
- Throughput guidance: Model A (7B, fp16) ≈ 450 tokens/s per rgpu-8; Model B (13B, q4) ≈ 210 tokens/s per rgpu-8 (numbers are workload-dependent; we provide private benchmarks on request under NDA).
- KV cache isolations: KV caches are per-cluster and never swapped across clusters; persisted caches can be disabled at request.
- Autoscale lead time: Recommended buffer of 10–15% reserved capacity for predictable burst; cold-start for new GPU machines may be 1–3 minutes depending on region and image pull.

Contract negotiation playbook (commercial rules of thumb):
- Minimum commercial offer: baseline committed monthly spend + 3-month ramp credit for onboarding.
- SLA redlines to accept internally: Cap the SLA credit at 50% of monthly commitment; cap per-incident credit to a single-day equivalent and aggregate monthly cap at 100% of monthly commitment only in extreme cases.
- Acceptable latency SLOs: Provide model-family p95 targets; avoid committing p99 unless product metrics team approves.
- Escalation for capacity events: Commit to "operational remediation" timelines (e.g., initial response 15 minutes, mitigation plan within 2 hours) instead of guaranteed time-to-recover.
- Pricing guardrails for burst: Bill burst at a premium (e.g., 1.5x baseline unit rate) or allow capped burst-hours per month included in commitment.

Procurement FAQ + suggested answers (for SEs):
Q: Can we audit the tenant isolation?
A: Yes — we provide SOC2 artefacts, configurable audit log retention, and (for enterprise purchases) can accommodate third-party security assessments and architecture walkthroughs.
Q: Do you allow termination for convenience with pro-rated refunds?
A: Standard dedicated contracts include a minimum commitment term; early termination language, pro-rata refunds, and wind-down assistance are negotiable for deals above X annual commitment.
Q: What happens if you deprecate a model we pin?
A: We commit to versioning and migration paths: customers can pin model versions; if a model is deprecated we offer a migration window with compatibility notes and assistance migrating to a compatible variant.

Competitive notes (short internal bullets — for SEs to emphasize in confrontations):
- Large cloud providers: strength = integrated infra and broad compliance; weakness = inconsistent per-token throughput numbers and lack of inference-specific runtime optimizations; negotiating SLAs across infra/ML layers is slower.
- Small LLM API vendors: strength = simple pricing and speed to start; weakness = limited procurement controls (no dedicated tenancy) and less transparency on per-route performance.
- Self-hosted runtimes: strength = full control; weakness = engineering burden, slower iteration, and higher TCO at scale.

Deal play and redlines (tactical suggestions for AE/SE):
- For mid-market deals (<$100k ARR): lean on standard SLA templates and limit custom clauses; offer 60–90 day onboarding at no charge for first deployment.
- For strategic enterprise (>= $500k ARR): allow contract redlines for audit and model-pin guarantees; include an SLO annex with explicit throughput targets and runbook commitments.
- When procurement pushes for unlimited burst: push back — require a burst-cap, premium rate, or explicit pre-approved windows.

Onboarding checklist for SOW (copyable):
- Kickoff and architecture review (1 week)
- Baseline capacity calibration & benchmark (2 weeks)
- Cluster provisioning & security hardening (1–2 weeks)
- Traffic migration & canary testing (2–4 weeks)
- SLA cutover and runbook handoff (1 week)
Total typical timeline: 6–10 weeks (depends on customer approvals and compliance checks).

Open questions / items for product to clarify (internal):
- Exact p95/p99 numbers for the three most common model sizes on the new rgpu-8 instance type.
- Clarify cold-start times for encrypted container images in EU regions.
- Standard wording for model-deprecation migration guarantee (legal/legal ops to produce templated clause).

Usage guidance for SEs: pasteable email snippet to procurement:
"Attached is our dedicated capacity RFI packet (includes SLA summary, onboarding timeline, and sample SOW). We can also provide a short architecture review call and run private benchmarks under NDA to validate throughput targets. Please let me know your procurement timeline and any mandatory contract clauses so we can align legal early." 

Appendix: quick checklist of measurable metrics procurement will ask for (for Solutions Engineers to collect ahead of negotiation):
- Committed monthly spend and baseline nodes
- Expected p95/p99 latency for key routes + seq length
- Sustained tokens/sec guarantee per cluster
- Burst policy (rate and duration) and charge model
- Incident response SLA and on-call numbers
- Audit log retention, KMS provider, SOC2/ISO artifacts

Last updated notes: this is an evergreen toolkit — update throughput numbers and product-specific wording before any enterprise RFx. If you change any SLA language, add the change to JIRA-1234 so legal and product are informed.
